inputs.share_count_basis: POST-SPLIT fully diluted: 979.49M basic at 2026-06-30 (Q2 2026 10-Q balance sheet, pre-split) + 9.8M dilutive awards (Q2 2026 diluted 988.48M less basic 978.66M), x2 for the 2-for-1 split effective 2026-08-11 (Yahoo split event 2:1 on that date; Q2 10-Q filed 2026-08-07 so every count in it, and every row in the Metrics CSV, is PRE-split). Cross-check: 1,978.6M x $43.6 (2026-09-22) = $86.2B = stockanalysis market cap that day. Held FLAT: SBC is fully expensed in the flows, so diluting the count as well would double-charge it; buybacks ($104M FY2025, $134M H1 2026) are the mechanism that keeps the count flat.
inputs.cash_note: Cash 2,192.4 + short-term investments 1,226.8 + long-term investments 781.3 at 2026-06-30 (Q2 2026 10-Q, XBRL ShortTermInvestments / LongTermInvestments). The 2024 revolver drawn for the $3B Dutch tender was fully repaid by Q2 2025; no LongTermDebt tag since. Operating lease liabilities (~$50M) are left in the flows as rent inside EBITDA and NOT added to net debt (treatment A).
inputs.sbc_source: TTM to 2026-06-30 = FY2025 10-K + H1 2026 10-Q - H1 2025 10-Q cash-flow add-back (ShareBasedCompensation: 125.687 + 63.965 - 53.854). Equity-award tax withholding (PaymentsRelatedToTaxWithholdingForShareBasedCompensation) is lumpy and immaterial on this window: $0.1M tagged for Q2 2026, nothing tagged for FY2025; FY2023's $214M and FY2024's $23M were exercise-driven one-offs. Monster publishes no combined figure, so the two lines are summed.
inputs.interest_income_note: Monster's income statement line is 'Interest and other income (expense), net' (XBRL OtherNonoperatingIncomeExpense): TTM 87.8 = 63.175 FY2025 + 47.997 H1 2026 - 23.337 H1 2025. It is stripped in full because net cash ($4.2B) is 2.2x the owner-FCF base. The line nets FX gains/losses against interest, so in low-rate years (2020-22) it was near zero or negative; the historical owner-FCF series uses the same net line each year.
inputs.buyback_note: FY2025 financing-activity repurchases $103.6M; H1 2026 $134.0M. The $3.77B in FY2024 was the one-off modified Dutch auction tender. Flat-count assumption is funded.
inputs.ttm_build: Revenue 8,294.3 (FY2025) + 4,890.8 (H1 2026) - 3,966.2 (H1 2025) = 9,219.0. Same construction for EBITDA (post-SBC 2,808.6; pre-SBC 2,944.4 = 31.9%), D&A 120.2 (1.30%), capex 140.8 (1.53%), OCF 2,238.8, reported FCF 2,098.0, net income 2,127.7, pretax 2,776.2, income tax expense 648.6 (23.4%), cash taxes paid 619.5 (22.3%). Using a TTM base ending on the balance-sheet date means no half-year of FCF is counted both in net cash and in year 1.
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows. Risk-free 4.2% (10y UST), ERP 5.0%, beta ~0.95 (low-beta consumer staple with growth-stock trading pattern) -> cost of equity 8.95%; zero debt so WACC = cost of equity, rounded to 9.0%. Same rate in all three scenarios: risk is carried in the scenario paths and weights, not stacked on the discount rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: A: operating leases (~$50M liability, immaterial against $4.2B cash) stay as rent inside EBITDA; lease liabilities excluded from net debt. No lease_cost_pct_path.
inputs.notes: Model: owner-FCF DCF, component build, 10-year horizon (growth is still decelerating from 20%+ toward terminal; margins are mature). Routed via dcf-methods SKILL.md row 1 (operating company, consumer). First valuation of this ticker; no memory entry. Adaptations file not needed: US filer, USD flows, no material leases, no NCI, SBC non-zero. SPLIT WARNING: the task brief stated the Metrics CSV share counts were already post-split; they are not. The Q2 2026 10-Q (filed 2026-08-07) predates the 2026-08-11 2-for-1 split and its 988.5M diluted count is pre-split -- using it against the post-split $42.14 price would double intrinsic value. Share count here is 2 x 989.3 = 1,978.6M. Adj EBITDA margin in this file is PRE-SBC (CSV EBITDA 2,808.6 TTM is post-SBC; + 135.8 SBC = 2,944.4 = 31.9%). Working capital capture is NEGATIVE (-6% of the revenue increase): a manufacturer/distributor with receivables + inventory > payables consumes cash as it grows (FY2023 -6%, FY2025 -6% of the YoY revenue increase; H1 2026 -17% seasonal). Cash tax 22.5% (TTM cash taxes 22.3% of pretax, GAAP 23.4%), ramped to 23%. Capex held at 2.0% of revenue, above the TTM 1.5% because management is adding co-packing capacity and upgrading Phoenix/Norwalk; D&A rises from 1.3% toward 1.7% as that capex depreciates. Implied exit multiples (~17x owner FCF base) are well below today's ~42x EV/owner-FCF -- the model assumes multiple compression, which is the finding, not an error.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: revenue_5yr_cagr (FY2020-FY2025); equity CAGR is not usable as the anchor because the $3.77B FY2024 tender removed ~$3B of book
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 3yr CAGR 5.5% is 42% below revenue 3yr 9.5% and 73% below EPS 3yr 20.1%: the FY2024 $3.77B Dutch-auction buyback shrank book value and the share count, so book-value compounding understates the business. FCF CAGRs are window artefacts: FY2022 was a working-capital/capex trough (owner FCF $635M on $6.3B revenue), so the 3yr owner-FCF CAGR of 41% is recovery, not trend; the 5yr figure (7.3%) is the honest one and sits below revenue growth because FY2020 was a cash-conversion peak. EPS is NI / diluted shares (CSV EPS column is blank from FY2016; FY2020 count doubled to the FY2021 post-split basis).
historical_growth.notes: Owner-FCF history (reported FCF - SBC - equity-award taxes - interest/other income, $M): FY2020 1,251; FY2021 1,024; FY2022 635; FY2023 1,098; FY2024 1,491; FY2025 1,777; TTM Jun-26 1,874. SBC has grown faster than cash flow (0.96% of revenue FY2023 -> 1.52% FY2025), and the FY2023 $214M withholding payment makes the owner series lumpier than the reported one.

base.narrative: Growth steps down from the TTM 23% as the FY2026 pricing round and the Strategic Brands transfer anniversary; international (46% of sales, +35%) keeps the company in double digits for three years, then the category matures toward nominal GDP. Adj EBITDA margin holds ~32% (TTM 31.9%, H1 2026 32.6%) with only 100bp of long-run recovery: Q4 2026 pricing offsets the 40% of aluminum tariff cost not mitigated, but Celsius/Alani competition caps the return to the 35-36% of 2018-19.

bull.narrative: International white space via the Coca-Cola system compounds at 25%+ for several more years, pricing sticks, aluminum normalises, and the margin recovers to the 35% of 2018-21. Alcohol is wound down or sold without further damage.

bear.narrative: US share keeps leaking to Celsius/Alani Nu in the female and wellness occasions, international decelerates once the Strategic Brands and pricing anniversaries pass, aluminum tariffs are only partly recovered, and a caffeine-labelling or product-liability outcome adds marketing restrictions. Revenue growth settles at 3% by year 4 and the margin compresses 350bp to 28.5%.

scenario_narratives.base: Monster keeps the #2 global position; international expansion (46% of sales, +35% YoY) sustains double-digit growth for ~3 years before the category matures; adj EBITDA margin holds at ~32% with pricing offsetting tariff-driven aluminum costs; capex 2% of revenue for co-packing capacity; terminal growth 3% at 9% WACC, Gordon-bound below the 20x cap.
scenario_narratives.bull: International compounds at 25%+ for longer, pricing power proves durable and aluminum costs normalise, lifting margins back to the 35% of 2018-21; growth stays double-digit for five years; terminal growth 3.5%.
scenario_narratives.bear: Celsius/Alani keep taking US share, international growth fades after the pricing and Strategic Brands anniversaries, only ~60% of the tariff cost is recovered, and regulatory/litigation pressure on caffeine content adds cost; growth settles at 3% by year 4 with margins 350bp lower; terminal growth 2%, 15x cap.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear lifted from the 15% house default to 20%: the category's fastest-growing segment is being won by challengers, the caffeine-content regulatory/litigation overhang is persistent rather than cyclical, and the stock enters the valuation at ~40x trailing earnings so a deceleration would be punished. Bull trimmed to 30% because it needs two independent things -- sustained 25%+ international growth AND a 300bp margin recovery -- to both come true. Balance-sheet risk is nil ($4.2B net cash, no debt), which is why bear is not higher.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Owner-FCF (SBC and interest income stripped, share count flat) discounted at a 9% USD cost of equity over a 10-year path in which growth decelerates from 20%+ to 3.5%; terminal value bounded by min(Gordon, 20x FCF). Net cash of $4.2B is added at the end, which is why the interest it earns is removed from the flows. The market price sits well above the house value: at $42 the stock discounts either a far longer runway of high-teens growth or a cost of capital nearer 7%; the required-return table says which.
key_risks_to_valuation: Share basis: every count in the filings and the CSV is pre-split; the model uses 2x. If a later refresh reads a post-split filing (Q3 2026 10-Q onward, ~1.96B basic), do not double again.
Terminal value is the bulk of the base-case value; each 1pp of WACC is worth roughly $4-5/share.
Growth path: the TTM 23% is flattered by the FY2025 Strategic Brands transfer and pricing; the model fades to 14% in year 1 -- if growth holds above 20% for two more years the base case is too low.
Margin: 32% assumes pricing covers the unmitigated 40% of aluminum tariff cost; a commodity spike without pricing is a 200-300bp hit (bear).
Working-capital capture at -6% of the revenue increase is a judgment from two clean years; H1 seasonality makes the half-year reads unreliable.
